newsitem.title: USA: Dynamics shareholder likes WHX's upped bid.
newsitem.headline: Dynamics shareholder likes WHX's upped bid.

text.p: One of Dynamics Corp's biggest shareholders endorsed WHX Corp's sweetened $45 offer for a bigger stake in Dynamics on Wednesday, a sign that Dynamics will likely accept the offer.

Analysts said Dynamics' decision on the offer -- $5 a share more than WHX's first bid on March 31 -- would depend on what its large shareholders, such as Mario Gabelli and Dimensional Funds, thought. Gabelli runs Gabelli Funds in Rye, New York, which owns about 20 percent of Dynamics' shares.

"It may not be a bad number," Gabelli, who bought his Dynamics shares at around $16 each, said of the $45 a share bid. "Essentially Ron Labow (WHX's chairman) has crafted a compelling bid for shareholders of Dynamics and clearly we're examining the bid.

"I don't see how Dynamics can ignore what its largest shareholders think," said Hope Crifo, an analyst at KDP Investment Advisors. She said that, if Dynamics ultimately balked at the second WHX offer, a third one of more than $45 a share was not out of the question.

Officials from WHX were not immediately available to comment. Dynamics said it would have a comment on the second offer by Monday. The Dimensional Fund said it does not comment on stocks it holds in its funds.

WHX's $45 a share offer Wednesday for another 649,000 shares -- or 17 percent -- of Dynamics values the Greenwich, Connecticut-based maker of electrical appliances and electronic devices at about $180 million -- $20 million more than its first, $40 a share bid.

WHX said its intention is to boost its current 2.9 percent stake in Dynamics to about 19.9 percent -- just under the 20 percent ownership level that would trigger Dynamics' shareholders rights plan, or "poison pill."

With greater ownership, WHX would then try to wrest control of Dynamics by naming new members to Dynamics' board and adopting by-laws permitting owners of more than a 9.9 percent stake to call special company meetings, analysts said.
WHX said it would seek to make any subsequent offers for Dynamics' remaining shares at $45 a share. Dynamics shares, however, closed Wednesday below the $45 a share offer at 44.
Some analysts took that as an indication investors believed the deal might not get done -- even if WHX were to boost its offer a third time.

One arbitrage trader pointed to WHX's unsuccessful bid last year for Teledyne Inc, which eventually merged with Allegheny Ludlum Corp. The trader said investors feared a Teledyne redux: WHX again would not come through.
Gabelli, for one, shrugged off that suggestion, saying that Dynamics -- in contrast to Teledyne -- is small enough for WHX -- with a storehouse of $400 million in cash -- to digest.
"The difference this time is size," Gabelli said. "And WHX definitely has the cash."
But, of course, after WHX's sweetend offer Wednesday -- so does Gabelli.

In addition to his 20 percent stake in Dynamics -- whose shares are up about $12 since March 31 -- Gabelli also owns 20 percent of CTS Corp, an electronics maker that is 44 percent owned by Dynamics, for his funds.
CTS' stock closed up 1-1/4 on WHX's sweetened Dynamics' offer at 56-1/2. The shares have risen almost seven points since WHX's March 31 offer for Dynamics.
